title: Same Tree
statement: You get the roots of two binary trees. Say whether they are the same: they must have exactly the same shape, and every pair of nodes in the same position must hold the same value.

example.caption: Same shape, but the last leaf is 3 in one tree and 4 in the other. Not the same.

idea.sentence: Walk both trees in step: at each spot the two nodes must both be missing or both hold the same value, and then both sides must match too.

jargon.plain: Which positions have a node and which are empty, ignoring the values.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: tree p and tree q, each a level-order array with null for a missing child, e.g. [1,2,3] and [1,2,3]

vars.meaning: number of nodes in the smaller tree

compare.bruteLabel: Write both trees out as lists, then compare the lists
compare.optimalLabel: Compare node pairs directly and stop at the first difference

rows.name: Serialize both, compare
rows.note: Needs a marker for empty spots, or different shapes can give the same list.

rows.name: Recursive pair walk
rows.note: Stops at the first mismatch. Memory is the call stack, one path deep.

fast.takeaway: Both are linear in the worst case. The pair walk needs no extra copy and quits the moment it finds a difference.

stages.title: Both empty
stages.note: Two missing nodes at the same spot match. Return true.

stages.title: Mismatch
stages.note: If only one node exists, or the two values differ, the trees are different. Return false.

stages.title: Match, go deeper
stages.note: This pair is equal. Both left sides must match and both right sides must match.

edges.title: Both empty
edges.why: Two empty trees are the same. The first check handles it.

edges.title: One empty
edges.why: One node exists and the other does not. This is the shape mismatch.

edges.title: Same values, different shape
edges.why: Both hold 1 and 2, but 2 is a left child in one and a right child in the other.

edges.title: Difference far down
edges.why: The top matches. You only find the mismatch by going all the way to the leaves.

gotchas.text: Check both-empty first. If you check one-empty first, two empty nodes are wrongly called a mismatch.
Comparing only the values (say, in-order lists) is not enough. Different shapes can give the same value list.
Missing children are null. Test with !p, never with p.val, which throws on null.
Compare pointers to nil before reading p.Val. Reading a field of a nil pointer panics.
Use && so the right side is skipped once the left side is false. That is the early exit.

recap.pattern: Tree recursion: two trees in step
recap.key: At each spot: both empty is a match, one empty or unequal values is a mismatch, otherwise both sides must match.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) call stack.
moves: One null or values differ: return false
